attribution.note: Zitron states this directly in his own argument.

semantics.note: The normalisation preserves the contemporaneous, industry-wide assertion of concentrated investment interest and the availability of revenue-generating alternatives.

contract.note: In this investment context, funding allocation is a fair ordinary test of the sweeping claim that venture focuses on AI and little else. July is a reasonable contemporaneous window, though allocation does not directly measure enthusiasm.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous global July data put AI at 11% of funding, with substantial funding in other sectors. This contradicts overwhelming concentration under the contract's allocation reading.
The July interview documents enthusiasm for AI but does not establish industry-wide concentration or little interest elsewhere. Earlier funding examples do not measure July allocation.

reviews.rationale: Under the fair funding-allocation reading, AI's 11% share and substantial funding elsewhere contradict the central concentration assertion. Investor enthusiasm does not establish near-exclusive investment focus. The merits and abundance of unspecified alternative companies remain unmeasured.
